topic: The Wallis Product: An Infinite Dance Toward Pi
target_audience: Undergraduate STEM students or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Sine Power Integral
lecture_lines: Let I sub n be the integral.
We integrate sine to the power n.
The area flattens as n increases.
animations: Display integral formula: I_n = ∫ sin^n(x) dx. (#FFFFFF)
Highlight exponent n in the integral formula. (#FF0000)

sections.title: The Recursive Ratio
lecture_lines: I sub n relates to I sub n minus 2.
The ratio of integrals approaches one.
animations: Demonstrate R_n approaches 1 as n grows. (#00FF00) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Deriving the Wallis Product
lecture_lines: Substitute integrals into our ratio formula.
Isolate pi over two through algebra.
animations: Display I_n formula for even n using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/calculator.svg]. (#FFFFFF)
Display I_n formula for odd n using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/notebook.svg]. (#FFFFFF)

sections.title: Visualizing Convergence
lecture_lines: Partial products oscillate around pi over two.

sections.title: Summary and Significance
lecture_lines: Calculus meets the circle constant pi.
A elegant dance toward the truth.
